articles.title: DESCRIBE THE EDIT. LET THE CREATIVE AGENT RUN IT ACROSS CREATIVE CLOUD
articles.summary: Adobe Firefly, the AI creative studio, brings Adobe's creative tools, top AI models and the Adobe Creative Agent together in one place. Through Firefly AI Assistant, powered by the Creative Agent, you can carry out multi-step creative tasks using Creative Cloud tools. Simply describe what you want to achieve, then work with the Creative Agent as your creative partner to guide and refine the results. With Plan Mode, you can preview and adjust the agent's approach before work begins, customize your creative preferences, and use Model Selector to choose your preferred AI model for each session. Learn more [5].

articles.title: JONY IVE AND MARGARET CALVERT CREATE POSTERS TO CELEBRATE DECADE OF DESIGN MUSEUM IN KENSINGTON
articles.summary: London's Design Museum has commissioned ten prominent designers to create posters celebrating the tenth anniversary of its move to Kensington in 2016. Jony Ive and LoveFrom contributed a minimalist gray-and-white composition resembling the number 10, while Margaret Calvert created a road sign-inspired design referencing the museum's former location at Shad Thames. Other contributors include Tim Burton, Hella Jongerius, Paul Smith, Marina Willer, and Tom Dixon, with designs spanning illustration, typography, textiles, and graphic design.

articles.title: GOOGLE WANTS ALL APPS TO BE FOLDABLE-READY, AND THE SHIFT GOES INTO EFFECT NEXT YEAR
articles.summary: Google Play will require Android apps to meet baseline foldable compatibility standards starting in April 2027, with noncompliant apps potentially losing the ability to publish updates. Apps must fill the available screen without letterboxing, preserve user activity when devices fold or rotate, and support multi-window operation. Developers will also need to provide foldable screenshots, while more advanced guidelines encourage responsive multi-pane layouts, external input support, and interfaces that adapt to different device postures.

articles.title: INTRODUCING STITCH LOOP: A NEW WAY TO BUILD AND EVOLVE PRODUCTS
articles.summary: Google Labs' Stitch Loop is a long-running product agent that connects to a codebase and live metrics to keep improving software after launch. It suggests fixes, writes code in a cloud sandbox, and opens GitHub pull requests, with nothing merging until a person approves. Built-in loops cover security, latency, and accessibility, and a global waitlist is open with priority for eligible Google AI Ultra users.

articles.title: AI MADE US FASTER. SO WHY DO DESIGNERS HAVE LESS TIME?
articles.summary: AI has dramatically reduced the time required to generate creative work, but designers often face shorter deadlines, more revisions, and an overwhelming number of options to evaluate. A study by METR in 2025 found that experienced developers took 19% longer to complete tasks with early-2025 AI tools despite believing they were working faster, illustrating the difference between perceived and actual productivity. The problem stems partly from adding AI to unchanged workflows, making deliberate constraints, faster selection methods, and stronger design fundamentals essential for realizing meaningful time savings.

articles.title: DESIGN LEADERSHIP IN 2026 IS MOSTLY SAYING NO TO GOOD IDEAS
articles.summary: AI has made prototyping inexpensive enough that designers, product managers, and engineers can generate numerous viable solutions, shifting design leadership toward evaluating ideas and deciding which ones deserve to ship. Leaders increasingly spend their time reviewing prototypes, protecting product priorities, aligning teams, and rejecting attractive features that would introduce unnecessary complexity or distract from the roadmap. As design and engineering roles converge, understanding business context, exercising judgment, and maintaining high standards become more important than simply producing polished interfaces.

articles.title: SEND THE FIREFIGHTERS TO THE FIRES
articles.summary: Enterprise interfaces frequently bury urgent problems inside enormous tables, forcing users to search through hundreds of records instead of immediately seeing what requires attention. Management by exception, a principle dating back more than a century, suggests that operational software should prioritize abnormal conditions and actionable issues while keeping healthy systems in the background. Designing around exceptions rather than exhaustive inventories can reduce cognitive load, accelerate problem resolution, and make dashboards more useful for the people responsible for fixing things.

articles.title: SHIP FRAMER SITES WITH ANY AI
articles.summary: Framer MCP connects ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor or Grok to Framer. Ask your agent for a landing page, a new blog post or a full site, and it builds it on the canvas, fills your CMS and publishes it live on your domain. It isn't code, an export, or a mockup: it's a real, editable Framer site you can review and tweak before you ship. It works wherever your AI tool runs, even your phone, and setup takes a minute.

articles.summary: Describe a video in chat and an AI agent animates it: kinetic type, 3D effects, and sound.

articles.title: TURN 3D INTO A LINK ANYONE CAN OPEN
articles.summary: Verse is the streaming layer for 3D. Any 3D world, from any source, opens as a link on any device: a floor plan, a 3D file, a design tool, or a game world.

articles.title: LONDON FILM SCHOOL: REBELLIOUS BRANDING BY RABBITHOLE
articles.summary: Rabbithole has redesigned London Film School's identity to reconnect the institution with the independent, anti-establishment spirit that defined its founding in 1956. The visual system combines Kimera's condensed Waldenburg typeface, a vivid red palette, and bold framing bars that evoke cinematic composition without relying on familiar film-related symbols. Modular layouts, animated typography, and stark contrasts extend across print materials, merchandise, and a redesigned website intended to communicate more clearly with prospective international students.

articles.title: ON DRAWING ICONS
articles.summary: Pierre has rebuilt its icon library from the ground up, creating more than 1,200 icons across three sizes and multiple variants to establish a more consistent visual language. The process involved refining stroke weights, optical alignment, proportions, and reusable shapes while developing custom Figma plugins to automate repetitive operations such as swapping layers, generating previews, and adjusting arrow geometry. The redesigned library also required a new pipeline connecting Figma, SVG, and React, demonstrating how careful visual craftsmanship and purpose-built tooling can work together to maintain consistency at scale.

articles.title: WHY I DON'T LIKE (AND DON'T RECOMMEND) WEBSITE CHECKLISTS
articles.summary: Website checklists are built for bulk, standardizing specifics instead of tailoring them, and every one contains advice that doesn't apply. A 2019 dissection of the front-end checklist ended with 41 thumbs-down and 13 raised hands. Quality websites are bespoke, so understanding the problem and knowing the craft matter more than any checklist, template, or framework.

articles.title: MINIMALISM VS. MAXIMALISM: FINDING THE RIGHT BALANCE FOR YOUR NEXT WEB DESIGN PROJECT
articles.summary: Web design swings between sterile minimalism and chaotic maximalism, yet neither extreme works on its own.

articles.summary: Callum Abbott's redesign of The Other Almanac used 40 typefaces and no new images.
